title: Cell types and organelles
blurb: Tell prokaryotic from eukaryotic and plant from animal cells, match every organelle to its job, trace a secreted protein, and explain how cells differentiate.
question: A lab slide shows three cells: one with no nucleus, one with a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole, and one packed with rough ER that exports an enzyme. What is each cell, which organelles explain its features, and why do cells with the same DNA end up so different?

teach.body: Cell theory states that all living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells come from pre-existing cells. Formal definitions: a prokaryotic cell (Bacteria, Archaea) has no nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles; a eukaryotic cell (protists, fungi, plants, animals) has a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles. Plain English: a prokaryote is a one-room cabin; a eukaryote is a building with separate departments. Both have a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA.

teach.caption: Prokaryotic cells are smaller than eukaryotic cells.
Both are eukaryotic. Plant cells have mitochondria AND chloroplasts: they respire as well as photosynthesize.
Note the rigid cell wall outside the membrane and the large central vacuole: animal cells have neither. Plant cells have mitochondria as well as chloroplasts.

Main job
Memory hook
teach.caption: The nucleus is wrapped in a double nuclear envelope with pores. Ribosomes are not membrane-bound; they float free or sit on rough ER.
Note the rough ER right beside the nucleus and the Golgi between the ER and the membrane: 1 to 4 follow the route a secreted protein takes.

Main job
rows: Break down fatty acids, toxins; catalase on H₂O₂
Store water, ions, wastes; turgor in plants
teach.caption: Lysosomes digest with acidic hydrolytic enzymes; peroxisomes detoxify with catalase.

teach.h: Power plants with their own DNA
teach.body: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration to make ATP; their inner membrane folds into cristae around a fluid matrix. Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis in thylakoids surrounded by stroma; chlorophyll is the pigment inside them. Both have double membranes, their own circular DNA and ribosomes, and divide independently. Endosymbiotic theory says both descend from prokaryotes engulfed by an ancestral cell.

Every body cell made by mitosis from the zygote carries the same DNA. Cells become specialized (differentiate) by switching on different genes, so each type makes its own proteins. Stem cells are unspecialized cells that can divide and differentiate: embryonic stem cells can become almost any cell type, while adult stem cells are more limited (bone marrow stem cells make blood cells). Structure matches function: a red blood cell has no nucleus and is packed with hemoglobin, a muscle cell has many mitochondria, a sperm has a flagellum.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Aisha reads three cells
teach.body: Aisha, a nursing applicant, studies a slide. Cell 1 has no nucleus, only a nucleoid and ribosomes: a prokaryote, such as a bacterium. Cell 2 has a cellulose wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole: a plant cell, which also has mitochondria. Cell 3, from the pancreas, is packed with rough ER and Golgi because it exports enzymes. A liver cell would show more smooth ER for detoxification. All her human cells share the same DNA; they differ because they express different genes.

teach.text: Look-alike traps: prokaryotes HAVE ribosomes and DNA but no nucleus; plant cells HAVE mitochondria; animal cells have no wall; ribosomes make PROTEINS and smooth ER makes LIPIDS; the Golgi packages proteins but does not make them; the nucleOLUS makes rRNA; bacterial walls are peptidoglycan, not cellulose; differentiated cells have the SAME DNA, expressed differently.

items: Prokaryotes: no nucleus or membrane organelles; ribosomes, DNA, membrane, cytoplasm present.
Plant cells: wall, chloroplasts, central vacuole, plus mitochondria. Animal cells: no wall, centrioles.
Ribosomes make protein; rough ER folds it; Golgi modifies and packages it; exocytosis releases it.
Smooth ER: lipids, steroids, detox. Lysosomes digest; peroxisomes use catalase.
Mitochondria (ATP) and chloroplasts (photosynthesis) have their own DNA: endosymbiosis.
Differentiation: same DNA, different genes expressed; stem cells can still specialize.

summary: You can now tell prokaryotic from eukaryotic cells and plant from animal cells, match each organelle to its function and trace a secreted protein from rough ER through the Golgi to exocytosis. You can also explain that differentiated cells share the same DNA but express different genes, and what makes stem cells special.

A.q: Which organelle modifies, sorts and packages proteins into vesicles for secretion or delivery?
A.why: The Golgi apparatus is the cell's post office: it modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles.

whyNot.0: Rough ER makes and folds proteins, then sends them on to the Golgi for finishing and packaging.
whyNot.2: Smooth ER makes lipids and steroids and detoxifies; it does not package proteins for export.
whyNot.3: Lysosomes digest materials with hydrolytic enzymes; they do not package exports.

A.q: Which structure is found in BOTH prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
A.why: Every cell needs to make proteins, so prokaryotes and eukaryotes both have ribosomes (along with DNA, cytoplasm and a plasma membrane).

whyNot.1: Prokaryotes have no nucleus, so they have no nuclear envelope.
whyNot.2: Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles, which prokaryotes lack.
whyNot.3: The Golgi is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotes.

A.q: Which structure inside the nucleus makes ribosomal RNA and assembles ribosome subunits?
A.why: The nucleolus, inside the nucleus, makes rRNA and assembles the ribosome subunits.

whyNot.0: The nuclear envelope is the double membrane with pores that surrounds the nucleus.
whyNot.1: Chromatin is the DNA-protein material that carries genes; it does not build ribosomes.
whyNot.3: The centrosome lies outside the nucleus and organizes microtubules for the spindle.

B.q: A pancreatic cell secretes a digestive enzyme. Which sequence shows the enzyme's path from synthesis to release?
options: Golgi → vesicle → rough ER → vesicle → membrane
Smooth ER → vesicle → Golgi → lysosome → membrane
Rough ER → vesicle → lysosome → Golgi → membrane
Rough ER → vesicle → Golgi → vesicle → membrane
B.why: Secreted proteins are made on rough ER, carried by a transport vesicle to the Golgi, then shipped in a secretory vesicle to the plasma membrane for exocytosis.

whyNot.0: The Golgi receives proteins from the ER; it does not send them back to the ER for export.
whyNot.1: Smooth ER has no ribosomes, and lysosomes digest material rather than deliver exports.
whyNot.2: Lysosomes are not a stop on the secretion route; the vesicle goes straight to the Golgi.

B.q: Which group of structures is found in a typical plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
B.why: A cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole mark a plant cell; animal cells have none of them.

whyNot.0: Animal cells also have mitochondria, so this group is not plant-only.
whyNot.2: Centrioles are typical of animal cells, and both cell types have ribosomes.
whyNot.3: Animal cells also have a nucleus and a cell membrane.

B.q: Which cell would you expect to contain the greatest number of mitochondria?
B.why: Mitochondria supply ATP, and heart muscle contracts continuously, so its cells are packed with mitochondria.

whyNot.0: Fat cells mainly store lipid and have a low energy demand.
whyNot.1: Surface skin cells have far lower energy needs than constantly contracting muscle.
whyNot.3: Cartilage cells are relatively inactive metabolically, so they need fewer mitochondria.

C.q: A patient's liver cells are repeatedly exposed to a drug that must be detoxified. Which organelle would these cells be expected to expand?
C.why: Smooth ER carries out detoxification in liver cells, so repeated drug exposure expands it.

whyNot.0: Rough ER makes and folds proteins; detoxification is a smooth ER job.
whyNot.1: The Golgi packages proteins for export; it does not detoxify drugs.
whyNot.2: Lysosomes digest worn-out organelles and engulfed material, not drugs dissolved in the cell.

C.q: Which statement about mitochondria is CORRECT?
options: They are absent from leaf and root cells.
They contain their own circular DNA.
They are found in bacterial cells.
They capture light to make glucose.
C.why: Mitochondria carry their own circular DNA and ribosomes, evidence for the endosymbiotic theory.

whyNot.0: Plant cells, including leaf and root cells, have mitochondria as well as chloroplasts.
whyNot.2: Bacteria are prokaryotes and have no membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria.
whyNot.3: Capturing light to make glucose is photosynthesis, which happens in chloroplasts.

C.q: A skin cell and a muscle cell from the same person look and work very differently. Which explanation is accurate?
options: They carry different sets of genes.
They express different sets of genes.
They lost the genes they do not use.
C.why: All of a person's body cells descend from one zygote and carry the same DNA; they differentiate by switching on different genes.

whyNot.0: The two cells carry the same DNA; only gene expression differs.
whyNot.2: Unused genes are switched off, not removed from the cell.
whyNot.3: All of one person's cells come from a single zygote.

reteach.title: The cell as a factory
reteach.question: Picture a factory that designs, builds and ships a product. Which department matches each organelle?

blocks.body: Head office (nucleus) keeps the master blueprints and sends out copies. The assembly line (ribosomes) builds the product. Finishing (rough ER) folds it into shape. The shipping department (Golgi) labels, sorts and boxes it. Delivery trucks (vesicles) carry it to the loading dock (plasma membrane). The power plant (mitochondria) keeps everything running, and the recycling crew (lysosomes) breaks down broken equipment. A prokaryote is a one-room workshop: same blueprints and assembly line, no separate departments.

blocks.text: Shipping does not build the product: the Golgi modifies and packages proteins, but ribosomes make them.

explain.body: Prokaryotes (Bacteria, Archaea) lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; their DNA sits in a nucleoid. Eukaryotes (protists, fungi, plants, animals) have both. Plant cells add a cellulose wall, chloroplasts and a central vacuole; fungi have chitin walls.

children.label: Eukaryote
children.sub: Wall + chloroplasts = plant; no wall = animal

test.q: A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria and a cell wall, but no chloroplasts. Which is its most likely source?
test.why: A nucleus and mitochondria make it eukaryotic; a wall without chloroplasts fits a fungus such as yeast.

whyNot.0: Bacteria are prokaryotes, with no nucleus or mitochondria.
whyNot.1: Animal cells such as liver cells have no cell wall.
whyNot.2: A leaf cell would contain chloroplasts.

explain.body: Ribosomes build proteins. Ribosomes on the rough ER make proteins for secretion, membranes and lysosomes; the rough ER folds them; the Golgi modifies, sorts and packages them into vesicles.

test.q: Which organelle is studded with ribosomes and folds proteins destined for secretion?
test.why: Rough ER is covered in ribosomes, giving it a rough look, and folds the proteins they make.

whyNot.0: Smooth ER has no ribosomes; it makes lipids and steroids.
whyNot.2: The Golgi receives proteins from the rough ER and packages them; it has no ribosomes.
whyNot.3: The nucleolus builds ribosome subunits but does not fold secreted proteins.

explain.body: Smooth ER makes lipids and steroids, detoxifies (especially in liver) and stores calcium. Lysosomes use acidic hydrolytic enzymes to digest worn-out organelles, food particles and engulfed bacteria. Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and toxins; catalase turns H₂O₂ into water and O₂.

test.q: A neutrophil engulfs a bacterium. Which organelle supplies the hydrolytic enzymes that digest it?
test.why: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes in an acidic interior and digest engulfed bacteria.

whyNot.0: Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and hydrogen peroxide, not engulfed bacteria.
whyNot.1: The Golgi makes lysosomes but does not itself digest engulfed material.
whyNot.2: Smooth ER detoxifies dissolved chemicals; it does not digest whole bacteria.

explain.body: Mitochondria make ATP by aerobic respiration (cristae, matrix). Chloroplasts do photosynthesis. Both have double membranes, their own DNA and ribosomes, and divide independently: the evidence for endosymbiotic theory.

test.q: Which feature of mitochondria supports the endosymbiotic theory?
options: Own circular DNA and a double membrane
A single outer membrane, like lysosomes
Division by mitosis with the nucleus
test.why: Their own circular DNA, double membrane and independent division all resemble an engulfed prokaryote.

whyNot.1: Mitochondria have a double membrane, not a single one.
whyNot.2: The Golgi makes lysosomes and vesicles, not mitochondria.
whyNot.3: Mitochondria divide on their own, separately from mitosis of the nucleus.

explain.body: Body cells share the same DNA but express different genes, so they make different proteins and take different shapes. Stem cells are unspecialized and can still divide and differentiate; adult stem cells, such as those in bone marrow, form a limited range of cell types.

test.q: Which feature defines a stem cell?
options: It has lost its nucleus and most organelles.
It carries more DNA than specialized cells.
It can divide and become specialized cells.
It is found in embryos but not in adults.
test.why: Stem cells are unspecialized cells that can divide and give rise to specialized cell types.

whyNot.0: Losing the nucleus describes a mature red blood cell, a fully specialized cell.
whyNot.1: Stem cells carry the same DNA as the body's other cells.
whyNot.3: Adults also have stem cells, such as those in bone marrow.
